projectBackground.name: Data Breach Response — Alder Health Clinics
projectBackground.context: A laptop with patient records was stolen. The clinic must decide what to report and to whom.

manager.name: Rachel Osei
manager.note: The clock starts when you become aware. Be fast, accurate and documented.

assignment.title: Manage the breach and strengthen compliance
assignment.brief: Apply deadlines, estimate exposure, choose lawful basis, spot DPIA triggers and draft the notification.

documents.name: Incident Report
documents.note: 12,500 records on a stolen laptop; 8% contain health data.

documents.name: New Project
documents.note: Clinic plans to analyse health data with a new AI tool.

tasks.title: Notification Deadline
tasks.prompt: Within how long must a personal data breach normally be notified to the regulator?
options: 72 hours after becoming aware, where there is a risk to individuals
tasks.mistake: Waiting for full investigation misses the deadline.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Maximum Fine
tasks.prompt: Maximum fine is the higher of €20M or 4% of turnover. Turnover is €300M. What is the cap (€ millions)?
tasks.mistake: Using 4% alone gives 12M, which is wrong.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Special Category Records
tasks.prompt: 8% of 12,500 records contain health data. How many records?
tasks.reasoning: Health data is special category data.
tasks.mistake: Treating all records alike underestimates harm.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Lawful Basis
tasks.prompt: Which is a lawful basis for processing patient data for care?
options: Provision of healthcare with a suitable condition for health data
tasks.reasoning: Basis and condition must both exist.
tasks.mistake: Using consent for everything can be wrong.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: DPIA Triggers
tasks.prompt: Select reasons a DPIA is required for the new AI project.
tasks.mistake: Skipping DPIA is a compliance failure.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Regulator Notification
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence breach notification summary.
tasks.modelAnswer: On 12 November a laptop containing 12,500 patient records, of which 1,000 include health data, was stolen from a clinic vehicle. The device was password-protected but not encrypted. We became aware on 12 November and are notifying within 72 hours. Affected individuals are being informed, and encryption of all devices has been ordered. A DPO contact is provided for queries.
tasks.reasoning: A good notification states facts, numbers, timing, mitigation and a contact.
tasks.tip: What, how many, when, fix, contact.
tasks.mistake: Late or vague notifications increase penalties.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Unencrypted Laptop
caseStudy.background: A hospital lost an unencrypted laptop and delayed notifying for three weeks. The regulator fined it for both lack of encryption and late notice.
caseStudy.challenges: No encryption policy and slow escalation.
caseStudy.constraints: Staff didn't know whom to tell.
caseStudy.solution: Kestrel built a breach playbook with a 24-hour internal escalation rule.
